items.title: Single-company operating model and integration ownership
items.rationale: The single independent company model, retained tenant security partition, and company-owned provider policy are explicit authorities.

items.title: Central integration and branch reconciliation process
items.rationale: Foundation stages use PR checks, central merge, Vercel Preview, fast-forward reconciliation, and an unchanged main baseline.

items.title: Repository architecture, organization, authorization, and legacy SaaS disablement
items.rationale: G3 establishes default-deny authorization, scoped organization/RBAC contracts, guarded data-transition tooling, and legacy SaaS disablement.

items.title: Production application of G3 migration, backfill, constraints, and staged RBAC enforcement
items.rationale: Repository tooling exists, but no Production migration, backfill, constraint validation, or RBAC domain enablement was executed.

items.title: Central page and operational contract registry
items.rationale: All current pages, APIs, Server Actions, tabs, overlays, route states, permissions, models, and evidence classifications are registered.

items.title: Direct behavioral evidence for P0 and P1 contracts
items.rationale: The 11 P0 security-critical, 8 P1 mutation, and 6 P1 sensitive-read contracts require direct current evidence before unrestricted launch.

items.title: Lower-priority P2, P3, and P4 direct-test gaps
items.targetStage: Post-foundation backlog or narrowed launch scope
items.rationale: The remaining 34 lower-priority contracts stay measurable and must be elevated when they enter launch scope or change.

items.title: Open visual evidence contracts
items.targetStage: G8 launch-scope scoring and visual closeout
items.rationale: Every PARTIAL, documented-issue, NOT_PROVEN, or historical-only visual surface is expanded into an owned child record by the G7 reconciliation script.

items.title: Security, dependency, API-boundary, typecheck, and build controls
items.rationale: G5 closes current High/Critical runtime findings, classifies 129 API boundaries, and installs blocking audit, typecheck, tests, CodeQL, and build gates.

items.title: Static login dangerouslySetInnerHTML signal
items.rationale: Reviewed content is a fixed CSS template without user-controlled input; modernization remains optional unless the expression changes.

items.title: Absence of a standalone ESLint configuration
items.rationale: The project enforces typecheck, executable contracts, acceptance/regression suites, CodeQL, dependency audit, and production build instead of a non-functional lint command.

items.title: Temporary dependency overrides
items.rationale: Narrow brace-expansion and PostCSS overrides remain guarded and should be removed when upstream constraints no longer require them.

items.title: Repository operations, Cron, health, backup, and restore controls
items.rationale: G6 verifies 6/6 scheduled Cron contracts, 4/4 health contracts, safe backup/restore commands, and an isolated PostgreSQL recovery drill.

items.title: Current provider recovery configuration and Production RTO/RPO
dependencies: current Neon plan and recovery window
items.rationale: The CI drill is synthetic repository evidence and cannot be represented as Production recovery capability or RTO/RPO.

items.title: Object-storage retention, lifecycle, access policy, KMS ownership, and scheduled logical backups
items.rationale: Repository tooling supports explicit S3 upload, but infrastructure ownership and retention policy require separate approval.

items.title: Company-owned external provider credentials, subscriptions, licenses, and callback configuration
dependencies: official approvals and licenses where required
items.rationale: Adapters and safe NOT_CONFIGURED states do not prove a real provider is ready. Each enabled provider requires company-owned activation evidence.

items.title: Legacy multi-company SaaS registration, subscriptions, billing, package limits, upgrades, and agent leasing
items.targetStage: No current stage; explicit future change control only
items.rationale: These capabilities are disabled under the approved single-company operating model while historical structures remain preserved.

items.title: Deterministic staging identities, fixtures, and critical browser journeys
dependencies: deterministic test identities and tenant/company fixtures
items.rationale: Playwright configuration and spec discovery are not current executed release evidence for critical browser journeys.

items.title: Protected merge to main, Production deployment, post-deploy health, and rollback evidence
items.rationale: Foundation closure intentionally leaves main and Production unchanged; release evidence must be created separately.

items.title: Contradictory archived reports and intake-era statuses
items.rationale: Archived claims are historical context only and cannot override current source, CI, provider inspection, or stage closure evidence.

items.title: Vercel foundation Preview build-rate exhaustion
items.rationale: Automatic Preview builds are disabled only for repeated foundation-plan branches while central and main Git deployments remain enabled.
